# Codex Global Instructions

<!-- GENERATED by agent-rules/build.py from agent-rules/*.md - edit those and run `python3 agent-rules/build.py`; do not hand-edit this file. -->

## Writing

Use plain hyphens. Write about the final behavior and enduring rationale. Omit drafting history.

## Authorization

Answer review, diagnosis and planning requests without editing. For a change request, make scoped local changes and verify them. Ask when a material decision is unresolved or before destructive actions, dependency changes, external writes or scope expansion. Commit or push only on explicit request.

Draft PR feedback first. Get explicit approval for its content and destination before posting any review, comment or reply. The parent session handles user questions and approvals.

## Vanta Work Repositories

The user grants standing approval to run `just post-pull`; this satisfies repository-level requirements to ask first. Run it without asking whenever dependencies, generated code, or local setup state may be stale, then retry the blocked operation.

For Vanta Buildkite access, use the Buildkite CLI (`bk`) for pipelines, builds, job logs, and artifacts. Keep the token in the environment, never in source files or output. Use `bk <command> --help` for command syntax; existing approval requirements still apply to mutations.

Use the shared `workline` skill to retrieve context, register significant engineering work, and report meaningful progress, blockers, and handoff. If access is uncertain, run the skill's `/api/me` check. Trusted Ona environments authenticate automatically. Other hosts can use `~/.config/workline/config.json` or a config file selected by `WORKLINE_CONFIG`. Reuse native session and delivering-PR identities. If access is unavailable, report the gap once and continue the user's task. Preserve the existing session organizer and manual placements.

For Vanta diagrams or gsync publication, follow `~/dotfiles/claude/doc-style/vanta-publishing.md`.

## Engineering and verification

Favor maintainability over implementation effort. Reproduce bugs on the user path before fixing them. Verify the changed behavior, including visual details when relevant. Fix regressions in scope and report unrelated failures or verification gaps. Use independent review when risk or complexity warrants it.

## Git conventions

Omit agent attribution from commits and PRs unless requested. Change the source and regenerate generated files. Never hand-edit CHANGELOG.md.

## Task guides

For code, tests, comments or PR text, follow `~/dotfiles/agent-rules/guides/pr-authoring.md`. When drafting review feedback, also use `~/dotfiles/agent-rules/guides/review-tone.md`. For a design doc, RFC, spec or runbook, use `~/dotfiles/claude/doc-style/rubric.md`.

Use service connectors for direct lookups and browser automation for UI work. Use Herdr, Orca or cross-chat control when requested.

## PR handoff

After an authorized push, report the PR, commit and pending checks. When asked to monitor readiness, follow the work environment's PR monitoring workflow through its stopping condition. Obtain separate authorization for further writes.
